stem: Under Article 26 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which kind of education "shall be compulsory"?
hints: Article 26 treats each level of education differently. Notice the word it uses for each level.
Recall the first paragraph of Article 26. It says one thing about elementary education, another about technical and professional education, and another about higher education.
Match each level to its word: "compulsory", "generally available" or "equally accessible ... on the basis of merit". Only one level gets the word in the question.

solution.methodName: Recall the exact words of the provision

steps.action: Find the provision: Article 26(1) of the UDHR.
Read the rule for elementary education: "Elementary education shall be compulsory."
steps.why: Compulsory means required. Everyone must take it.

steps.action: Read the rule for technical and professional education: it "shall be made generally available".
steps.why: "Generally available" means it should be offered to people, not that everyone must take it.

steps.action: Read the rule for higher education: it "shall be equally accessible to all on the basis of merit".
steps.why: "On the basis of merit" means entry depends on ability, so it is not required of everyone.

steps.action: Only elementary education is called compulsory. The answer is elementary education.

trapNotes.Higher education: Article 26 says higher education "shall be equally accessible to all on the basis of merit". Open to all by merit is not the same as compulsory.
trapNotes.Technical and professional education: Article 26 says technical and professional education "shall be made generally available". Available is not compulsory.
trapNotes.All levels of education: Article 26 makes only elementary education compulsory. The other levels are to be available or accessible, not required.

sourceRef.citation: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 26(1)
